title: Precision routing and cost-estimation playbook for pricing & billing requests
creator: Aisha Patel
description: A compact, operational playbook for intake, prioritization, and routing of non-bug customer requests related to pricing, commitments, invoicing, cost allocation, and marketplace transactions. Focused goals: (1) apply a reproducible scoring model to quickly classify impact and priority; (2) route requests to the right owner (Finance, Partnerships, Sales/CS, Product, Legal); (3) produce consistent initial cost impact estimates and recommended short vs long-term actions; (4) define SLAs for customer responses and unblockers for high-impact cases.
context_and_goals: Problem: ad-hoc handling of pricing and billing asks causes slow SLAs, inconsistent decisions, and downstream finance/accounting rework.
Goal 1: Reduce first-touch routing time to < 8 business hours for P0/P1 requests.
Goal 2: Provide a one-page cost impact estimate and recommended action set within 3 business days for P1 requests.
Goal 3: Capture decision rationale and permanent outcome in the ticket (closure template) to build an institutional knowledge base.

Scope: Commitments (reserved capacity/discounts), invoicing disputes and cadence changes, cost allocation tagging, marketplace revenue split adjustments, and non-bug pricing/packaging product asks. Not in scope: incidents, technical production outages, or legal contract negotiation drafts (Legal consults are routed as dependency).
intake_form_template: Customer / Account name (with Redwood account ID if available):
Request type (pick one): commitments | invoice | cost_allocation | marketplace | pricing_change | refund | credit_policy
Estimated MRR/ARR impact or one-time value (USD):
Is there a signed contract or commitment reference? (yes/no + link):
Requested due date or customer SLA:
Attachments: invoice PDF, screenshots, contract excerpt, marketplace agreement, billing export link
triage_scoring_model: - Customer tier (0 self-serve / 1 Small / 2 Mid-market / 3 Enterprise):
- Revenue impact (0 none / 1 <5k / 2 5k-50k / 3 >50k monthly or >250k one-time):
- Operational risk (0 workaround trivial / 1 minor friction / 2 billing inaccuracies / 3 regulatory/audit/legal exposure):
- Time sensitivity (0 flexible / 1 within 2 weeks / 2 within 72 hours / 3 immediate SLA breach):
- 12-15 => P0 (Immediate exec attention, 24-48h response, finance + sales + product):
- 9-11 => P1 (High, respond within 8 business hours, remedy or temporary credit within 3 business days):
- 5-8 => P2 (Medium, evaluate within 5 business days and schedule implementation in next sprint or billing cycle):
- 0-4 => P3 (Low, standard backlog grooming and PM prioritization).
routing_rules: If request_type == commitments => route to: Product (Pricing) + Sales Operations + Finance. Attach contract link and commitment tier. If score >= 9 include Exec AE and CS lead in thread.

If request_type == invoice => route to: Billing Ops (Finance) + CS. For disputed invoices include the invoice PDF and customer's stated disputed amount. If regulatory/audit tag present, add Legal and Compliance.
If request_type == cost_allocation => route to: Finance + Customer Platform (if tagging requires instrumentation) + Product to verify feature gaps.

If request_type == marketplace => route to: Partnerships + Finance + Product (Marketplace). Include partner agreement and desired revenue split change. If >50k impact, include Partnerships Director for approval.
If request includes contract/legal terms or proposed changes => assign Legal as dependency and set security_review_required=true for documentation.
required_initial_artifacts: Minimum required on ticket before first triage: intake form completed, customer identifier, supporting attachments (invoice/contract), customer's requested due date, and score calculation documented.
If any artifact missing at first touch, triage engineer/PM must request it in the first reply and mark ticket as Blocked for routing until provided (max 3 business days).
routing_slAs: P0: acknowledge in Slack/email within 2 business hours, initial mitigation or temporary credit decision within 24-48 hours, final resolution target 7 calendar days unless legal dependencies exist.
P1: acknowledge within 8 business hours, cost impact estimate and recommended action within 3 business days, final resolution target depends on complexity but expected within 14 calendar days.
P2: acknowledge within 3 business days, include in next planning cycle (30 days) and provide timeline to the customer.
P3: acknowledge within 10 business days, triage into general backlog.
cost_impact_quick_estimate_guide: Purpose: give CS/Sales an initial order-of-magnitude to avoid escalations while Finance performs formal calculations.
- Reserved commitment discount estimate: use committed GPU-hour baseline x proposed discount %, translate to monthly cost delta. For small deals < $10k, use 20-30% discount cap without exec approval.
- One-time credits/refunds: limit recommended by CS: up to $5k without lead approval; $5k-50k requires Finance + Sales Ops sign-off; >$50k requires Director approval and finance journal entry plan.

- Marketplace rev share changes: calculate incremental revenue to Redwood and to partner over next 12 months; if partner revenue share reduction increases Redwood revenue > $50k ARR, route to Partnerships Director for approval.
Documentation: attach a spreadsheet snapshot with assumptions (billing period, quantities, exchange rates, amortization if necessary).
decision_and_approval_flow: - PM recommends action (short-term credit, pricing adjustment, contract amendment).
- Sales Ops validates customer-specific billing data.
- Finance approves accounting treatment (credit, invoice reissue, revenue recognition impact).
- Legal signs off on contract wording and retains redline evidence.
- > $50k or changes to T&Cs: Finance Director + Legal + Partnerships Director (if marketplace)
Record approvals as explicit comments in the ticket with approver name, title, and timestamp. Attach signed amendment if required.
closure_template: Customer communication excerpts (copy of message sent to customer):
Follow-up actions (if product work required, reference feature ticket key):
Retention: add tag for knowledge base if this is a recurring/novel edge case.
escrow_and_rollback_guidance: When issuing credits or reissuing invoices, ensure Finance has a rollback plan: journal entries, GL codes, and partner settlement adjustments (if marketplace involved).
For commitment changes that affect reserved compute, coordinate with Dedicated operations to ensure capacity and billing mapping do not create orphaned discounts.
metrics_to_track: Mean time to resolution for P0/P1
% of requests with complete intake on first touch
Number of re-opened billing tickets per quarter
Financial variance attributable to ad-hoc credits (monthly total)
Percentage of marketplace revenue-share edits requiring director approval
open_risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Finance bandwidth is limited during month-end causing SLA breaches. Mitigation: defer non-time-sensitive items and escalate P0/P1 to on-call Finance lead.
Risk: Lack of standard instrumentation for cost_allocation requests. Mitigation: include Product request for tagging UI and a dedicated engineering story to add exportable allocations.
Risk: Sales teams bypassing intake form. Mitigation: require intake form link in the shared CS playbook and enforce triage gate before Finance action.
acceptance_criteria: Playbook published as canonical doc and linked from CS/AE onboarding materials.
Triage form deployed as a template in Zendesk/Linear intake with required fields enforced.
Routing automations configured (initial Slack routing to SRE/Finance/Partnerships channels based on request type).
A dashboard tracking the metrics above (MTTA, MTTR by priority, incomplete intake %) exists and is reviewed weekly during Commercial Ops sync.
implementation_plan: Week 1: Finalize playbook text, create Linear ticket template and Zendesk form, circulate to stakeholders for review.
Week 2: Implement routing automations and Slack notifications; create initial dashboard queries.
Week 3: Pilot with 2 AE/CS teams for 2 weeks, capture feedback and refine scoring thresholds.
Week 4: Launch broadly, conduct 30-day review and iterate.
